profile.reading:
Switch Las Vegas 7 sits at 7135 South Decatur Boulevard, Las Vegas, Nevada, in unincorporated Enterprise, Clark County. Data center industry aggregators place its opening year at 2008, and Switch's own February 2014 press release for the neighboring SUPERNAP 8 building describes Las Vegas 7 as "the original SUPERNAP," sitting several hundred yards away, corroborating that this building was the founding structure of what became Switch's sprawling Core Campus. Switch's own company overview page confirms Las Vegas 7 by name alongside a newer Las Vegas 8 building as current facilities on the same Nevada campus. Switch does not publish individual square footage, megawatt capacity, or redundancy design figures for Las Vegas 7 on its current site. Its historical role as the company's first purpose built Las Vegas data center, from which the campus later expanded to include Las Vegas 4, 5, 8, 9, 10, 11, 12, and 14 among numbered buildings, is documented only indirectly through Switch's references to it in later press releases about newer buildings.

Switch was founded in 2000 by Rob Roy, who serves as the company's founder and chief executive and whom Switch credits with more than 950 issued and pending patent claims underlying its data center designs. Switch describes itself on its own site as a technology infrastructure ecosystem company whose core business is designing, building, and operating advanced data centers, and its company materials describe an operating philosophy it calls KARMA, built on the idea that putting good energy into the world and its surrounding communities brings good energy back to the company. Switch's Core Campus is marketed today as offering up to 495 megawatts of power upon completion and 100 percent renewable energy, with Nevada's consumer use tax and property tax abatement program, administered through the state's Governor's Office of Economic Development, cited by Switch as a business advantage of locating in Nevada, though this registry did not find a Switch specific abatement dollar figure published through that program.

Clark County's data center cluster, anchored substantially by Switch's Core Campus that Las Vegas 7 helped originate, has helped establish Las Vegas as a significant secondary US data center market outside the major coastal and Northern Virginia hubs. Switch has since built a large solar and battery storage generation program, including the Switch Station 1 and Switch Station 2 projects and the more recent Gigawatt Nevada development, to support its stated 100 percent renewable energy claim across its Nevada campuses, a program that traces its roots to the original site Las Vegas 7 anchors. Switch does not publish tenant identities for any of its numbered Las Vegas buildings, including this one, as is standard industry practice for large colocation and hyperscale campuses.

reading.body:
Switch Las Vegas 7, opened in 2008 on South Decatur Boulevard in unincorporated Enterprise, is the founding structure of Switch's sprawling Core Campus in Clark County, Nevada, and anchors what has grown into one of the secondary US data center markets outside coastal and Northern Virginia hubs. The operator does not publish individual megawatt capacity, square footage, or redundancy specifications for this building. Its historical significance rests on being the original SUPERNAP facility from which the campus later expanded to include at least eight additional numbered buildings, a role documented indirectly through Switch's references to Las Vegas 7 in press releases about newer structures on the same site.

The Core Campus as a whole is marketed as capable of delivering up to 495 megawatts of power and operating on 100 percent renewable energy once complete, though building-level specifications are not disclosed. Las Vegas 7's current contribution to that total capacity is not published by the operator. Switch describes itself as a technology infrastructure company founded on designs originating from this site, and the company has built a generation program including solar, battery storage, and the Gigawatt Nevada development to support its renewable energy claims across Nevada campuses.

In Nevada's measured data center landscape, only two facilities publish megawatt figures to this registry, totaling 10.37 MW of disclosed capacity across 26 mapped sites in the state. This campus ranks third by published megawatt capacity within Nevada despite Las Vegas 7's individual specs remaining unpublished, indicating that other unnamed Switch structures on the Core Campus or sister Nevada sites carry the published figures. Tenant identities for Las Vegas 7 are not disclosed, following standard industry practice for large colocation and hyperscale facilities.
